OWNED FILES: storygame/runtime/fixed_refusal.py (new), storygame/runtime/jev_questions.py, storygame/runtime/capture.py, bench/core.py (edit); tests/test_fixed_refusal.py (new), tests/test_bench_runtime_mode.py (edit). Edit nothing else. Do NOT edit storygame/web_demo.py or storygame/runtime/engine.py (production stays off).

PROBLEM: the narrator writes that a fixed thing (world.schema.is_fixed: the workstation, back door, drawer, truck seats) was carried or moved, and capture then refuses the move; the player keeps false prose. We are testing a PREVENTION step in the style of the existing prerequisite steps (storygame/runtime/taking.py take_before_put, seating.py board_vehicle / seat_before_use / stand_before_leave). Study take_before_put and its result dataclass first and copy its shape.

REQUIRED CHANGE (opt-in, default OFF):
1. jev_questions.py: add `relocates_thing(ask, command, thing_name) -> bool | None` next to moves_thing, same structure (noul question, uses _answer). Instructions text (plain words): 'Relocating a thing means the command lifts it, picks it up, carries it, drags it, pushes it, slides it, takes it out or off of where it is, removes it, detaches it, or puts it somewhere else.' Criteria true: 'The command makes the player relocate this thing.' Criteria false: 'The command uses the thing where it is: opening, closing, sitting in, looking at, reading, or searching it. It also covers a command that moves some other thing onto, into, off, or out of this thing.'
2. New file storygame/runtime/fixed_refusal.py with a frozen dataclass `FixedRefusalResult(command: str, steps: tuple[str, ...], asked: bool, issues: tuple[str, ...], refused: tuple[str, ...])` and `refuse_fixed_move(world, package, player_input, relocates_thing) -> FixedRefusalResult` where relocates_thing is Callable[[str, str], bool | None]. Candidates: items in package.world.items that are fixed (`world.schema.is_fixed(item_id)` or `item.fixed`), visible (`world.is_visible`), not an area (`world.is_a(id, 'area')` false), and in the same area as the protagonist (`world.area(item_id) == world.area(package.protagonist_id)`, both not None), sorted by id; skip any whose names the command does not mention (`_command_names_thing(player_input, world.names(item_id))` imported from storygame.runtime.seating). For each remaining candidate ask `relocates_thing(player_input, name)` once (asked=True). True: append the step sentence f"{protagonist} tried to move {article name}. It is fixed in place and did not move." (reuse `_protagonist_name` and `_with_article` from storygame/runtime/taking.py) and append the thing's name to `refused`. False: nothing. None: append issue f"fixed move question unanswered for '{name}'" and add no step. The world is NOT changed by this function. `command` is the steps joined with the player input (as TakingResult does).
3. capture.py: `WorldCapture.__init__(self, provider, ask, fixed_refusal: bool = False)`; store it. In `before_turn`, when self.fixed_refusal is true, call refuse_fixed_move FIRST (with `lambda c, t: relocates_thing(adapter, c, t)`). If it produced steps, do NOT call stand_before_leave, board_vehicle, take_before_put or seat_before_use (a refused carry must not board the truck or seat the player); use empty result objects of the same types those functions return (look at their dataclasses) so the rest of the method and the record dict are unchanged. `provider_steps` becomes (*fixed.steps, *standing.steps, *boarding_steps, *taking.steps, *seating_steps). When fixed_refusal is false, behaviour must be byte-identical to today and relocates_thing must never be called. Add to the returned record: 'fixed_refusal_steps' (list), 'fixed_refusal_asked' (bool), 'fixed_refusal_issues' (list), and include the issues in record['issues'] and the asked flag in record['asked'] as 'fixed_refusal'. No new persistent state: prior_steps is already saved and restored.
4. bench/core.py: both `WorldCapture(...)` construction sites (run_scene and the reload factory) pass `fixed_refusal=bool(variation.get('fixed_refusal', False))`. Where the bench copies the capture record's per-turn fields (such as standing_steps, taking_steps) into the turn record, also copy fixed_refusal_steps, fixed_refusal_asked and fixed_refusal_issues. Add 'fixed_refusal' to the variation hash payload only when true.

TESTS (hermetic, no network, no live worker; stub the ask callable): tests/test_fixed_refusal.py with the real package data/stories/continuity-initiative scene 1A (build the world the way tests/test_runtime_capture.py and tests/test_unknown_identity_not_creation.py do). Cases: (a) 'Carry the workstation to the truck.' with relocates stub True gives exactly one step 'Kristin tried to move the workstation. It is fixed in place and did not move.' and refused == ('workstation',); (b) stub False gives no step; (c) stub returning None gives the unanswered issue and no step; (d) a movable thing (Kristin's laptop) is never asked about; (e) a command that does not name the fixed thing asks nothing; (f) two fixed things named (workstation and back door) give two steps and two asks; (g) the world is unchanged afterwards (compare world.parent of the workstation before and after); (h) WorldCapture with fixed_refusal=True and a stub ask that says yes to relocates: before_turn's record['steps'][0] is the refusal sentence, provider.prior_steps starts with it, and the stand/board/take/seat questions are NOT asked (use an ask stub that records which question keys were requested and fail the test if any of the other four keys appear); (i) WorldCapture with default fixed_refusal=False never requests the relocates_thing key; (j) a jev_questions test that relocates_thing returns True/False/None for stub answers like the existing moves_thing tests. tests/test_bench_runtime_mode.py: add a test that a runtime-mode variation with fixed_refusal true builds a WorldCapture with fixed_refusal True and absent gives False (follow the existing monkeypatch pattern there). If a case cannot be built as described, adapt to the nearest real behaviour and say so in notes; never weaken (h) or (i).

HOW TO RUN: confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside the cwd. Tests: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov tests/test_fixed_refusal.py tests/test_bench_runtime_mode.py tests/test_runtime_capture.py tests/test_refusal_modes.py tests/test_web_demo.py. Also `-k "bench or capture or taking or seating or jev or item_facts"` over tests/. Ruff: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix and -m ruff format on every file you changed. Reply with the files changed.
